messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: CC data in R/qtl2 format
parts:
I've added some mouse Collaborative Cross genotype data in R/qtl2 format, at https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data.
The data are taken from the supplemental data for Srivastava et al. (2017) Genetics 206:537-556, https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.116.198838

There are still some problems. For example, CC037 is indicated in the Srivastava et al. (2017) supplemental data to have Y chromosome from the founder strain NOD, and to also have a large portion of the X chromosome from NOD. But the way R/qtl2 handles 8-way RIL, this should not happen.

karl

messages.author: 1504d994a3b46924
messages.subject: Re: CC data in R/qtl2 format
parts:
Karl,

Thank you for posting this data. I'm setting up an eQTL run for CC mice and would like to know if I'm using a valid approach. 
My study design has 22 CC strains, all of which are represented in the Srivastava data, and 3 diets. 

Assumptions that I made:

- cross$geno, cross$founder_geno, and cross$cross_info should be subset to my strains but otherwise unaltered.

- covariate matrix could be added with
 > cross$covar <- covariateMatrix
 
- expression matrix could be added with  
> cross$pheno <- expressionMatrix
 
- the different diets could be represented in cross$pheno with a suffix
 e.g CC001/Unc_Diet1; CC001/Unc_Diet2; CC001/Unc_Diet3

- cross$geno and cross$cross_info are the same regardless of diet, so we replicate the data for the same strains when adding in the different diet samples. 

check_cross2 returns TRUE before adding in pseudomarkers using the following parameters: https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/blob/master/CC/R/calc_genoprob.R

I finished by using the modified cross2 to make gpr, apr, and kLOCO. 

Appreciate your guidance as always,

Excel

Personally, I prefer not to answer questions of the form "is this a valid approach"?
I'm not comfortable serving as a rubber stamp for analyses when I'm not involved as a collaborator.

For the R/qtl2 list, I think it would be better to have more narrowly-focused questions, particularly regarding the software.

sorry,
karl
